source.title: Caring babies: Concern for others in distress during infancy.

confidence_rationale: Longitudinal study (n=165, 3 to 18 months) finds empathic concern already present at 3 months, moderately consistent across situations and ages, growing only modestly, and predicting later prosocial behaviour. This refutes the classic stage account (self-distress contagion first, other-oriented concern later) that a self-stream-routing developmental story would most naturally predict, yet early concern is compatible with an early-available fast routing mechanism. Observational coding of infant affect limits how finely concern can be separated from contagion.
failure_signatures: Coding 'concern' versus 'self-distress' from infant facial and vocal behaviour is inferential; early concern could partly be undetected contagion.
Does not measure the mechanism; it constrains the developmental timeline only.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Concern for distressed others appears early in the first year (from 3 months), is moderately consistent across situations and age, increases only modestly and plateaus in the second year, while prosocial behaviour rises sharply in the second year; early concern predicts later prosocial behaviour, contradicting stage theories in which concern emerges late from self-focused distress.
mapping.ree_translation: Constrains the developmental reading of MECH-405 (EMP-7 lit-pull). If other-bound affect is the own suffering stream routed through an other-model, and the other-model must be stable first (the claim's gate on ARC-083/OBJ-5), one would expect a period of undifferentiated contagion before other-oriented concern. Infants instead show other-oriented concern early, with little self-distress (see also Roth-Hanania et al. 2011), and it is prosocial ACTION, not concern, that grows later.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Either (a) a rudimentary other-model is available very early, in which case the gate is weaker than 'stable other-model', or (b) early concern does not require the routing mechanism at all. The data cannot separate these; they do weaken the specific contagion-to-concern sequence.
mapping.source_context: Israeli longitudinal cohort, observed responses to maternal, peer and stranger distress simulations at 3, 6, 12, 18 months.

confidence_components.notes: Good longitudinal design; mapping to a routing mechanism is indirect; relevant mainly to developmental gating assumptions.
